domain: 建构文化研究 (Studies in Tectonic Culture)

concepts.name: 建构 (Tectonics)
concepts.description: The art and science of construction, emphasizing the expressive potential of structure and joinery.

sub_concepts.name: 建造诗学 (Poetics of construction)
sub_concepts.description: The expressive and poetic articulation of structural elements.

sub_concepts.name: 核心形式 (Kernform)
sub_concepts.description: The structural and technical core of a building element.

sub_concepts.name: 艺术形式 (Kunstform)
sub_concepts.description: The symbolic, representational, and aesthetic aspect of a building element.

concepts.name: 建筑艺术四要素 (Four elements of architecture)
concepts.description: Gottfried Semper's classification of architecture into earthwork, hearth, framework/roof, and enclosing membrane.

sub_concepts.name: 构架体系 (Tectonics of the frame)
sub_concepts.description: Lightweight, linear elements joined to form a spatial matrix.

sub_concepts.name: 砌体结构 (Stereotomics of the earthwork)

concepts.name: 移情 (Empathy / Formgefühl)
concepts.description: The psychological projection of human feeling into architectural form.

concepts.name: 本体形式 (Ontological form)
concepts.description: The inherent truth and necessity of a form derived from its material and making.

concepts.name: 节点崇拜 (Adoration of the joint)
concepts.description: The articulation of connections as the primary locus of architectural meaning.

concepts.name: 材料置换理论 (Stoffwechseltheorie)
concepts.description: Semper's theory that formal motifs persist across changes in physical materials over time.

concepts.name: 地形学与场所 (Topography and Place)
concepts.description: The anchoring of architecture into its specific cultural and physical ground.

concepts.name: 身体性想像 (Metaphorical process of the body)
concepts.description: Understanding architectural elements through analogy to the human body.

concepts.name: 织理性建构 (Text-ile Tectonic)
concepts.description: The origins of enclosing walls in weaving and textile arts.

concepts.name: 古典理性主义 (Classical Rationalism)
concepts.description: The logical, structural tradition underlying neoclassical architecture.
